standard.title: Equivalent Representations of Rational Numbers
standard.description: find equivalent representations of rational numbers and represent rational numbers on a number line
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can compare and order fractions using equivalence, add and subtract fractions, and convert between simple fractions and decimals (from AC9M6N03, AC9M6N04, AC9M6N07). Students understand percentage as parts per hundred.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students find equivalent representations of rational numbers across fraction, decimal and percentage forms, simplify fractions, and place positive and negative fractions and mixed numerals on a number line.

nodes.label: Equivalence and simplification of fractions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students find equivalent fractions using common multiples and express fractions in simplest form using common divisors.
nodes.minimum_width: Find two equivalent fractions for a given fraction and simplify a fraction to its lowest terms.
nodes.typical_width: Use the fraction wall and number line to verify equivalence; apply simplification in computation contexts.
wider: Investigate what the simplest form of a fraction tells you about the relationship between numerator and denominator (coprime numbers).
Connect simplification to GCD from AC9M7N02: simplest form means GCD(numerator, denominator) = 1.

response_modes.reason: Fraction equivalence and simplification underpin every subsequent operation with rational numbers. Precision here matters — small errors in simplification compound.

nodes.hinge_reason: Simplification errors propagate into every subsequent conversion and operation with rational numbers — Node 2 conversions, Node 3 number line placement, and all of AC9M7N06 depend on fractions being in comparable forms.
success_criteria: Generates multiple equivalent fractions for a given fraction.
Correctly simplifies a fraction to lowest terms.
Can explain why the fractions are equivalent (multiplying/dividing numerator and denominator by the same value).

nodes.label: Converting between fraction, decimal and percentage
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students convert fluently between fraction, decimal and percentage representations of rational numbers.
nodes.minimum_width: Convert a given rational number between all three representations (fraction, decimal, percentage) for common values.
nodes.typical_width: Explain the conversion process for each direction; identify equivalent representations for less familiar fractions (e.g. 3/8 = 0.375 = 37.5%).
wider: Investigate repeating decimals (e.g. 1/3 = 0.333...) and understand these as rational numbers.
Explore how percentage, decimal and fraction choices affect ease of computation in different contexts.

response_modes.reason: Students often have strong conversion skills in one direction (fraction to decimal) but poor skills in others. Encountering the same rational number across varied contexts and conversion directions resolves partial understanding.

success_criteria: Correctly converts a given rational number between fraction, decimal and percentage forms.
Identifies when representations are equivalent without performing full conversion.
Does not confuse 0.5 with 5% (confusing decimal and percentage forms).
nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Repeating decimals and the density of rationals are genuinely rich extensions — advancing students who encounter 1/3 = 0.333... and reason about what this means are engaging with number structure beyond procedural conversion.

nodes.label: Rational numbers on the number line
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students place positive and negative fractions, decimals and mixed numerals accurately on a number line, including intervals other than 0–1.
nodes.minimum_width: Plot a given set of positive and negative fractions and mixed numerals on a number line with appropriate scale.
nodes.typical_width: Construct a number line for a given interval, select appropriate scale, and place a mixed set of rational numbers including fractions, decimals and percentages on it.
wider: Given a number line with some rational numbers marked, identify and justify the positions of unlabelled points.
Explore density of rational numbers: between any two rational numbers, find another — repeat and discuss what this implies.

response_modes.reason: Placing negative fractions requires a reasoning scaffold: students must convert to a comparable form and reason about which direction is more negative. Without explicit steps, students often mirror positive fractions incorrectly.

success_criteria: Correctly places a given set of rational numbers (including negatives and mixed numerals) on a number line.
Selects and labels appropriate scale for the interval.
Correctly orders the set from least to greatest.
